**Merge** creates a merge commit combining two branches. Both lineages stay in history. Result: tree branched and rejoined.

**Rebase** replays your commits on top of target branch. Rewrites history. Result: single linear line.

**When to merge:**
- Public/shared branches (main, develop, release)
- Team collaboration — rewriting history breaks others' work
- Want to preserve "when did this feature branch land" marker

**When to rebase:**
- Local feature branches before push
- Want clean, linear history in main
- Syncing with main while developing (rebase, don't merge)

**Golden rule:** Never rebase commits already pushed to shared branch. Rebase only unpublished work.

**Common flow:**
```
# Keep feature branch synced with main
git rebase main

# Push to origin (safe if branch is yours only)
git push -f origin feature

# Before PR merge, rebase if main moved ahead
git rebase main

# Merge PR with merge commit (or squash)
# Main stays clean, PR shows as single commit or merge bubble
```

**Why both exist:** Rebase = clean. Merge = safe for shared branches. Use rebase for your work, merge when sharing.
